signals.title: CHF/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Policy Divergence
signals.text: CHF/JPY trades at 188.92 as the weekly G10 strength scorecard confirms an extreme bilateral divergence, with JPY averaging +0.997% across 7 pairs while CHF drops −0.759% across 6 pairs, generating an actionable 1.756% spread. The underlying central bank dynamic reinforces the move: the BoJ policy rate sits at 1.25% against the SNB at 0.00%, establishing a 125bp carry advantage favoring JPY. JPY speculative positioning shows net long +4,472 contracts at the 98th percentile of its 52-week range (z +2.66), contrasting sharply with CHF net short −18,620 contracts pegged at the 2nd percentile (z −2.30). Furthermore, BEER valuation shows CHF/JPY cheap at z = −1.92σ below model fair value of 195.84. Trade bias: Bearish CHF/JPY, tracking institutional JPY outperformance against structural CHF weakness. Catalyst: BoJ Summary of Opinions and Tankan survey release at 23:50 UTC. Risk: Spread compresses below 0.80% if Swiss CPI surprises firmly to the upside.

signals.title: AUD/USD — CB Hike Surprise + Positioning Unwind
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.6996 following the RBA decision to raise the cash rate by 25bp to 4.60%, breaking below psychological support despite the hawkish move. The rate hike widens the cash differential 4.00% policy rate to 60bp, while the AONIA-SOFR OIS differential provides a 45bp carry advantage to AUD. However, technical posture remains impaired with spot trading below its SMA20 (0.7134), SMA50 (0.7096), and SMA200 (0.7028) cluster. Leveraged funds hold +55,684 net long contracts at the 81st percentile of the 52-week distribution, and the failure to hold gains post-decision exposes long liquidation risk. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/USD, fade the hawkish hike on technical breakdown below 0.7000. Catalyst: US Core PCE Price Index at 12:30 UTC. Risk: Daily close back above the SMA200 at 0.7028 invalidates the immediate breakdown thesis.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew vs Realized Vol Divergence
signals.text: USD/JPY prints at 157.45, hovering between the SMA20 at 156.28 and the descending SMA50/200 resistance band at 158.45/158.49. Saxo Bank 25-delta risk reversals exhibit an extreme put skew of −2.57, demonstrating heavy institutional demand for downside protection despite a +267bp SOFR vs TONA carry advantage supporting USD. Options 1M ATM implied volatility sits at 9.1% against 30-day realized volatility of 10.1%, yielding a negative volatility risk premium of −1.1%. Cross-asset signals show MOVE at the 98th percentile of its trailing year while VIX sits at the 28th percentile, highlighting elevated rates volatility that threatens elevated carry positions. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY, downside hedging pressure limits spot advancement toward 158.50. Catalyst: BoJ Summary of Opinions and Tankan survey at 23:50 UTC. Risk: Spot penetration through 158.50 unwinds put skew demand.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Yield Spread Drag + Technical Breakdown
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1364, remaining pinned beneath its descending technical barrier defined by the SMA20 at 1.1526, SMA50 at 1.1538, and SMA200 at 1.1622. The Fed policy rate at 4.00% vs ECB at 2.65% maintains a 135bp rate spread favoring USD, matched by a +146bp SOFR over €STR carry advantage. The US 5-year yield has widened +25bp over the trailing 5 sessions (FRED, as of Sep 24), split as real yield +24bp and breakeven +1bp, reflecting a real-yield-led driver underpinning the dollar. CFTC data reflects Leveraged Funds net short −58,805 contracts (19th percentile, z −1.01), showing sustained institutional alignment with downward momentum. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD, structural yield divergence caps recovery attempts. Catalyst: German Preliminary CPI at 12:00 UTC. Risk: Rebound through the 1.1450 intraday pivot challenges the bearish trend structure.
